title: Enigma Raises $71 Million: Making Robot Control as Simple as Turning a Volume Knob

content_html:
Another robotics company has entered the "embodied intelligence" field, one of the hardest challenges in AI - how to teach models to do tasks that no one has ever specifically taught them. The approaches vary widely: some analyze millions of online videos, others run computer simulations, and some embed sensors in gloves to collect human movements. Enigma, which emerged from hiding on Monday, took a completely different path: instead of focusing solely on model capabilities, it is studying how humans and machines interact, hoping to develop intuitive interfaces and even a different kind of machine brain from these interactions.

To fund this journey, Enigma raised a $71 million seed round led by Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital, with Sarah Guo from Conviction Partners also investing. This startup, less than a year old, aims to first understand how humans want to communicate with machines.

To bring this question into the real world, Enigma is launching a large-scale online experiment: anyone around the world can go online and interact with its 100 or so self-developed AI robots. These robots reside in garages located in Israel and California, capable of painting with brushes, fighting with swords, and lifting beakers to mix liquids for simple chemical experiments. Enigma claims that from the robotic arms to the underlying models, everything is built from scratch.

The company's two co-founders are like childhood friends. Jonathan Jacoby was once called the youngest employee at Microsoft - he was personally recruited by Wiz founder Assaf Rappaport when he was young; his friendship with Guy Nave began when they competed in hacking competitions as teenagers, later working together in Israel's elite 8200 unit on cybersecurity research, becoming close friends. When the two decided to start a business last year, they deliberately chose the field of robotics - a domain they were not experts in, but one that is known for containing the most fascinating unsolved problems in the tech world. They gathered a group of people from the Israeli tech circle whom Jacoby called "the smartest friends" - people from top AI labs, math competition gold medalists, and even a few who had been convinced to drop out of their doctoral programs.

Shardul Shah, a partner at Index Ventures, was particularly impressed by this "outsider" spirit: "Insiders may start with teleoperation or dexterity, but Enigma asks a very different question - what should the ultimate experience be?" In Jacoby's view, the interaction between humans and robots should be effortless. He gave a heart-wrenching example: if washing dishes required spending 15 minutes explaining where each item should go, people would just say "forget it, I'll do it myself" - and right now, even the most advanced models are still stuck on this point. He believes that dealing with robots should eventually be as intuitive as turning the volume knob on a car: no one likes to adjust the volume with percentages, yet they don't know whether the result is too loud or too quiet.

content_html_zh:
另一家机器人公司已经进入“体现智能”领域，这是人工智能中最困难的挑战之一——如何教模型完成从未有人专门教过它们的任务。 这些方法差异很大：一些分析数百万个在线视频，另一些运行计算机模拟，还有一些在手套中嵌入传感器来收集人体动作。 周一从隐藏中脱颖而出的 Enigma 走了一条完全不同的道路：它不再仅仅关注模型能力，而是研究人类和机器如何交互，希望从这些交互中开发出直观的界面，甚至是不同类型的机器大脑。

为了资助这一旅程，Enigma 筹集了由 Index Ventures 和 Ribbit Capital 领投的 7100 万美元种子轮融资，Conviction Partners 的 SarahGuo 也参与了投资。 这家成立还不到一年的初创公司旨在首先了解人类如何与机器沟通。

为了将这个问题带入现实世界，Enigma正在启动一项大规模的在线实验：世界各地的任何人都可以上网并与其100多个自主研发的AI机器人进行互动。 这些机器人驻留在以色列和加利福尼亚州的车库里，能够用画笔绘画、用剑战斗，以及举起烧杯混合液体进行简单的化学实验。 Enigma 声称，从机械臂到底层模型，一切都是从头开始构建的。

该公司的两位联合创始人就像儿时好友。 乔纳森·雅各比（Jonathan Jacoby）曾被称为微软最年轻的员工——他年轻时就被Wiz创始人阿萨夫·拉帕波特（Assaf Rappaport）亲自招募；他与 Guy Nave 的友谊始于青少年时期参加黑客比赛时，后来在以色列精英 8200 单位一起从事网络安全研究，成为了亲密的朋友。 当两人去年决定创业时，他们特意选择了机器人领域——他们并不是这个领域的专家，但这个领域以包含科技界最令人着迷的未解决问题而闻名。 他们聚集了一群来自以色列科技圈的人，雅各比称他们为“最聪明的朋友”——来自顶级人工智能实验室的人、数学竞赛金牌得主，甚至还有一些被说服放弃博士课程的人。

Index Ventures 的合伙人 Shardul Shah 对这种“局外人”精神印象特别深刻：“局内人可能会从远程操作或灵巧开始，但 Enigma 提出了一个非常不同的问题——最终的体验应该是什么？” 在雅各比看来，人类和机器人之间的互动应该是毫不费力的。 他举了一个令人心痛的例子：如果洗碗需要花15分钟解释每件物品应该放在哪里，人们只会说“算了，我自己来吧”——而现在，即使是最先进的模型也仍然停留在这一点上。 他认为，处理机器人最终应该像转动汽车上的音量旋钮一样直观：没有人喜欢用百分比调整音量，但他们不知道结果是否太大声或太安静。
